notable_anecdotes: John Gokongwei's three birthday donation milestones: P200M to ADMU on his 80th, P250M to DLSU on his 85th, and multiple school gifts on his 90th -- a systematic birthday-giving pattern.
Hans Sy relaying his father Henry's mandate to set up 50 NU campuses or affiliates nationwide -- a rare glimpse into dynastic philanthropic succession.
Toyota Japan matching George Ty's P1B endowment to the Toyota Institute of Technology peso-for-peso -- totaling P2B for one technical school.
Ayala's 'Affordable Private Education Centers' -- 27 centers preparing about 10,000 high school enrollees for higher-paying jobs -- as a systemic alternative to traditional scholarship giving.
Author's brief FLP note: three programs cosponsored by Metrobank (Professorial Chairs), Tan Yan Kee (law scholarships), and Ayala (dissertation contest) -- the column's only self-referential moment.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban surveys Philippine tycoons' preferred philanthropy -- education -- noting the irony that even those without college degrees devote personal and corporate funds to it. He catalogues school owners: Ramon del Rosario Jr.'s Phinma Group (four provincial schools); Lucio Tan (UE); Henry Sy (NU and Asia Pacific); Alfonso Yuchengco (Mapua); Emilio Yap heirs (CEU); Lourdes Reyes Montinola and son Aurelio Montinola III (FEU); George Ty (Tytana, plus P1B to Toyota Institute matched peso-for-peso by Toyota Japan). George Ty's Metrobank Foundation has become 'legendary' for its annual P1M Search for Outstanding Teachers prizes. Henry Sy mandated son Hans to build 50 NU campuses nationwide and recently constructed the new 9-story UP Professional Schools Building at Fort Bonifacio. John Gokongwei donated P200M to ADMU on his 80th birthday, P250M to DLSU on his 85th, and several gifts on his 90th. The Ayala brothers set up 27 Affordable Private Education Centers preparing 10,000 high school enrollees for higher-paying jobs, develop OJT curricula with universities, and co-founded AIM with the Lopezes and Washington SyCip. The Rufino family funded the DLSU Rufino campus at Fort Bonifacio. Manuel V. Pangilinan donated multiple buildings to Ateneo, San Beda, and St. Scholastica's and channeled multiple foundations toward education and vocational training. Ramon S. Ang's San Miguel Foundation funds agricultural and vocational scholarships, a child-nutrition program, and book donations to public schools. The Jollibee Group Foundation's 'Busog, Lusog, Talino' project serves thousands of schoolchildren. The column closes with the author noting that FLP's three education programs -- CJ Panganiban Professorial Chairs, Libpros law scholarships, and the legal dissertation contest -- are respectively cosponsored by Metrobank, Tan Yan Kee, and Ayala.
